newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco delays appeal of Briton jailed for drugs.
newsitem.headline: Morocco delays appeal of Briton jailed for drugs.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Wednesday put off for one week hearing an appeal by Briton David Richards, who was jailed for five years for drug trafficking while on holiday with his family.

The Moroccan news agency MAP said Richards appeared briefly before Tangiers Appeal Court and asked to put his case in writing to the prosecutor. He was told to submit the letter to the prison authorities.
Richards, 37, from Alnwick, Northumberland, was arrested with his wife Jill, 40, last August while embarking from Tangier for Spain with their eight-year-old daughter Victoria.

A Tangier court sentenced David Richards, who pleaded guilty, to five years and fined him 47,000 dirhams ($5,400). It acquitted Jill Richards who pleaded not guilty. She and her daughter later flew to Briton.
The court also ordered the seizure of the couple's vehicle in which 222-kg (489 pounds) of cannabis resin was found. ($1=8.7 dirhams)
